Shanghai giant Jin Jiang Hotels accelerates Southeast Asia expansion; HK's Portier Hotels rolls out new brand in Bali
article:
Asia Pacific’s hospitality sector is seeing sustained momentum with more hotels debuting.

Chinese hospitality behemoth Shanghai Jin Jiang International Hotels, for one, is picking up the pace in its expansion across Southeast Asia.

Separately, Hong Kong boutique player Portier Hotels has also launched a fresh collection of lifestyle hotels, The Arc House, starting with a property in Indonesia.

Jin Jiang Hotels is bringing six brands from China to the Southeast Asian market: Ginco Hotel, Renjoy Hotel, Metropole Jinjiang Hotels, Jinjiang Inn, Lavande, and 7 Days Premium.

These brands cover all segments, from economy to high-end products, to adapt to the diverse markets in the region.

In a Nov 12 press release, the Shanghai-listed global hotel group said the construction and rollout of its Southeast Asia projects are “advancing steadily”, and it is growing its regional footprint amid the tourism boom.

It most recently opened the 7 Days Premium Hotel in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, in July 2026. Next in the line-up is the Jinjiang Metropolo Hotels Luang Prabang in Laos, with its grand opening slated for Nov 16.

And in the first half of 2027, the 7 Days Premium Hotel in Jakarta, Indonesia, along with the Renjoy property and a second 7 Days project in Malaysia, will open successively.

Juvena He, general manager of overseas business, Jin Jiang Hotels China Region, pointed to the group’s “belief in Southeast Asia’s boundless potential” and long-term commitment to the region.

To date, Jin Jiang Hotels has three regional offices across Malaysia, Indonesia and Vietnam, with local employees accounting for more than 80% of its workforce.

These offices will work closely with Louvre Hotels Group, a subsidiary of Jin Jiang Hotels, to jointly deepen their footprint in Southeast Asia. Louvre Hotels Group manages over 1,750 properties in 70 countries, through brands such as Première Classe, Hosho, Kyriad, Campanile, Tulip Hotels & Residences, and Sarovar.

Jin Jiang Hotels ranks as the second-largest hotel group in the world by property count and the largest in Asia by room count. As at end-2025, it had invested in or managed more than 14,900 hotels with over 1.51 million rooms in more than a hundred countries.

New boutique lifestyle hotel brand, The Arc House

Meanwhile, Hong Kong-headquartered full-service boutique hospitality group Portier Hotels has introduced The Arc House — a collection of design-forward boutique lifestyle hotels.

The first property under the brand is the newly opened The Arc House Canggu on the southern coast of Bali, Indonesia.

Located near Batu Bolong Beach, the hotel in the Canggu resort village sits within a mix of contemporary dining, independent retail, wellness and nightlife options.

It has 19 suite villas with private pools, alongside an Indo-Japanese restaurant Mykaza, a rooftop infinity pool and wellness programming.

The collection will next expand to Hong Kong later this year with 24 rooms, followed by Melbourne, Australia, in early 2027 with 43 rooms.

In Hong Kong, the property will open at 148 Wellington Street, placing guests close to Central’s art, heritage, dining and city rhythms. This will also feature a lounge, rooftop terrace, gym and a Cantonese restaurant named One Forty Eight Wellington.

The Arc House aims to cater to travellers who want to feel closer to the character of a destination, according to a press release in early November 2026.

Each hotel under The Arc House brand will be shaped by its setting. Edward McKenna, co-founder of Portier Hotels, highlighted that Asia Pacific is a region of “very different travel cultures”, and increasingly guests expect hotels to reflect that richness.

“They look for design, service and food that bring them closer to a place, rather than offering the same experience in every destination,” he added.

In June, EdgeProp Singapore reported that lifestyle hotels — design-led properties that trade standardised comfort for local character, experiential programming and social spaces — are getting more popular in the region amid rising demand from Gen Z and a growing pool of conversion-ready assets .

Real estate consultancy CBRE had said then that lifestyle hotels are among the fastest-growing segments in the global hospitality industry, though such brands are still underpenetrated within Asia Pacific.

In terms of its design language, The Arc House features minimalist interiors and arches. In Canggu, the hotel also showcases locally sourced and commissioned artwork.

Portier Hotels was founded in 2023 and its offerings span hospitality development, operations and management, with properties in Asia Pacific. Besides The Arc House, the group’s portfolio has another brand known as je ne sais quoi.

title: Weaker 2H2026 for CDL as asset sales delayed; offices, malls stay strong
article:
City Developments (CDL) expects its financial performance for 2H2026 to be "significantly weaker" y-o-y, mainly due to the absence of divestment gains. In 2H2025, it booked a $473.1 million gain from the sale of its 50.1% stake in South Beach Consortium to joint venture partner IOI Properties Group .

Capital recycling deals CDL had planned for the rest of FY2026 are now expected to be completed in FY2027, due to "prevailing market conditions with persistent inflationary pressures and elevated interest rates".

Two other factors add to the drag. The Korean won's appreciation against the Singapore dollar since July has resulted in significant foreign exchange losses at CDL's Korean subsidiary, which holds an SGD-denominated intercompany loan receivable.

CDL is also revaluing its property portfolio, which may lead to impairment losses.

The firm’s 3Q2026 operational update was released after market close on Nov 11, when its shares ended the day at $7.12. In early trading the next day, they fell as much as 10.1% to a one-year low of $6.40, before paring losses. By Friday, Nov 13, the shares had closed at $6.64, down 6.7% over the two trading days.

Despite the weaker outlook, its operating assets are holding up. Its offices and luxury retail continue to outperform the wider market, and its Singapore hotels are busier, though rising costs are squeezing margins.

Offices, malls outperform market

CDL's Singapore office portfolio was 97.4% committed as at Sept 30, against an islandwide occupancy rate of 90.0%, based on URA data for 3Q2026. Republic Plaza was 98.0% committed and City House 96.8%. The portfolio has recorded positive rental reversions for three consecutive quarters this year.

The group's two Grade A office developments, Newport Tower and Union Square Central, are on track for completion in 2027 and 2028, respectively. CDL says both are drawing leasing interest from cybersecurity, fintech, financial and professional services firms. It expects tighter Grade A office supply over the next few years to support leasing.

The group's Singapore retail portfolio was 97.1% committed, compared with URA's islandwide rate of 93.5% for 3Q2026. City Square Mall was 97.3% committed, while Palais Renaissance on Orchard Road reached full occupancy, up from 98.6% as at June 30.

Tenant sales at Palais Renaissance rose 71.3% y-o-y, which CDL attributes to stronger spending among its luxury-fashion tenants.

Busier hotels, asset enhancements

For 9M2026, revenue per available room (RevPAR) at CDL's Singapore hotels rose 3.0% y-o-y to $163.3, as occupancy rose 2.7 percentage points to 81.2%. Average room rates (ARR) were broadly flat. CDL says the February Singapore Airshow boosted event-led international visitation.

Yet the Singapore hotels' gross operating profit (GOP) margin fell 2.5 percentage points to 36.4%, as operating costs outpaced revenue.

Two of its Singapore hotels are being refurbished. The 415-room M Hotel Singapore began a phased renovation of its guestrooms and public areas in May, with completion scheduled for 3Q2027.

At the 311-room Copthorne King's Hotel, the tender for refurbishing 169 rooms and public areas in the main wing has been completed. Major works are expected to run from 1Q2027 to 4Q2027.

The refurbishments extend beyond Singapore. In London, a major AEI at the 222-room Millennium Hotel London Knightsbridge is scheduled to start in 4Q2026.

The 833-room Copthorne Tara Hotel London Kensington began the first of three phases of room renovation in October, with the full programme due to be completed by 2Q2029.

In New York, the 124-room Millennium Premier Hotel New York Times Square reopened on June 1 after renovating its guestrooms and public areas. Renovation works at the adjacent 626-room Millennium Hotel Broadway Times Square is due to finish by 4Q2026 for its restaurant and public areas, and by 2H2028 for its rooms.

CDL is also adding a new hotel in the US. The 263-room M Social Hotel Sunnyvale in California is under construction and is expected to open in December 2026.

For 9M2026, group-wide hotel RevPAR rose 6.4% to $175.2, driven by a 2.3 percentage-point rise in occupancy to 75.2% and a 3.1% increase in ARR.

CDL expects RevPAR growth to continue through the rest of 2026, citing event-led demand from the Formula 1 Singapore Grand Prix in October, London's World Travel Market in November and BTS's four-night Singapore concert series in December.

Living sector: some stabilised, some still leasing up

CDL's living sector portfolio spans private rented sector (PRS) housing in Japan, the UK and Australia, and purpose-built student accommodation (PBSA) in the UK.

In Japan, its PRS portfolio of 40 assets and 2,246 units maintained occupancy above 95%. CDL says sustained wage growth and constrained new supply continue to support rental growth.

In the UK, The Junction in Leeds (665 units) was 94% occupied.

Newer assets are still filling up. The Octagon in Birmingham (370 units), which began operations in August 2025, was 56% occupied. The Archive in Melbourne, CDL's first operational PRS asset in Australia, was 65% occupied, with stabilisation expected in 2027.

Its UK PBSA portfolio of six properties and 2,368 beds was 83% occupied as at Sept 30 for the 2026/2027 academic year.

More assets are coming on stream. The YardHouse in London (209 units) reached practical completion in October, and leasing has begun. The Joinery in Manchester (261 units) is expected to complete in 1Q2027.

Gearing at 75%

CDL's net gearing, after factoring in the fair value of investment properties, stood at 75% as at Sept 30.

The group attributes this mainly to capital deployed for the Tanjong Rhu Road and Peck Hay Road government land sales (GLS) sites it won in 1H2026.

In February, a 90:10 joint venture between CDL and Woh Hup won the 131,743 sq ft Tanjong Rhu Road site with a $709.3 million bid, or $1,455 psf per plot ratio (psf ppr). It is slated for a 520-unit, 99-year leasehold condo across three 26-storey blocks with waterfront views. In June, CDL and Hong Realty, a member of Hong Leong Group, won the Peck Hay Road site with a $542.4 million bid ($1,865 psf ppr). The prime District 9 site can be developed into a 39-storey residential tower with 380 units.

Interest cover was 2.7 times. CDL had cash reserves of $2.1 billion, and $4.8 billion in cash and available committed credit facilities.

CDL says it remains committed to GET+, the three-year roadmap for FY2027 to FY2029 it unveiled on Sept 28 following its strategic review. The plan targets $6 billion in divestments, a reduction of about $3 billion in net borrowings and net gearing of about 55% by FY2029.

The group also aims to grow total assets under management across its listed and private platforms to $10 billion. One route it has outlined is seeding suitable assets into managed vehicles.

title: Top Stock Market Highlights of the Week: Nvidia, SGX, US Treasury Yields and Singapore’s Pension Ranking
article:
Welcome to this week’s edition of top stock market highlights.
A chipmaker that was the world’s most valuable company just weeks ago lost its long-time leader this week, and its shares tumbled.
Closer to home, market volatility lifted the local bourse’s derivatives trading volume to a six-month high in October.
Meanwhile, US bond yields climbed back above 5% as investors braced for more interest rate hikes.
And in a bright spot for Singapore, a global pension index ranked the country’s retirement system the best in Asia.
Nvidia’s CEO resigns as scandal deepens
Nvidia
(NASDAQ: NVDA) announced on 12 November 2026 that co-founder and
CEO Jensen Huang
had resigned following reports of two affairs.
Scrutiny began after Huang admitted to a relationship with a former executive at Singapore-based data centre firm Megaspeed International.
US authorities suspect her of spying for China, a claim Beijing has denied.
A later report said Huang had also had a relationship with a senior Nvidia executive who reported to him.
Chief financial officer Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO while the board searches for a permanent successor.
Board member Harvey Jones has been appointed Nvidia’s first-ever chair.
Huang, who owns about 3.6% of the company, will also leave the board.
The shares fell as much as 14% at the open, pushing Nvidia’s market capitalisation below US$4 trillion for the first time since 2025.
The stock is now roughly 35% below its early-October record, and at least seven Wall Street firms have downgraded it over the past week.
Investors will look to Nvidia’s 3QFY2027 results, due on 17 November 2026, for clarity.
Market volatility lifts SGX’s trading volumes
Singapore Exchange
(SGX: S68) reported on 12 November 2026 that its derivatives daily average volume climbed to a six-month high in October, as volatile markets drove demand for hedging.
Daily average derivatives volume rose 8% year on year and 17% month on month to 1.6 million contracts. FTSE China A50 Index Futures recorded a 24-month high in daily average volume.
Open interest (the value of contracts still outstanding) in GIFT Nifty 50 contracts topped US$20 billion.
Securities market turnover also rose, climbing 32% year on year to S$44.8 billion.
Daily average value reached S$2 billion, driven by trading in index stocks and REITs.
The pick-up came as Singapore shares weakened in October.
The
Straits Times Index
(SGX: ^STI) fell about 5% to 5,376.74, while the FTSE ST Technology Index dropped 17%.
Even so, the STI ended the month 21% higher than a year earlier.
US bond yields climb as bets on rate hikes grow
US Treasury yields rose sharply on 12 November 2026, with the benchmark 10-year yield climbing back above 5% to 5.068%.
The two-year yield, which is more sensitive to Federal Reserve policy, jumped more than 11 basis points (0.11 percentage point) to 4.843%.
Hotter-than-expected consumer price index (CPI) data earlier in the week strengthened expectations of further rate hikes.
Traders are now fully pricing in a hike in December, and
Goldman Sachs
(NYSE: GS) added another quarter-point hike in March 2027 to its forecast.
Oil added to
inflation
worries after President Donald Trump said the US does not need a deal with Iran.
That raised concerns the war in the Middle East could drag on, and Brent crude rose about 1% to US$93.60 a barrel.
Higher rates are already weighing on rate-sensitive sectors.
US existing home sales fell to their lowest level in more than 16 years in October.
For Singapore investors, rising rates could mean higher borrowing costs for REITs.
The impact on local banks is more mixed, as the 3Q2026 results for
DBS Group Holdings Ltd
(SGX: D05),
Oversea-Chinese Banking Corporation Limited
(SGX: O39) and
United Overseas Bank Limited
(SGX: U11
)
showed.
Singapore’s retirement system ranks first in Asia
Singapore’s
retirement
system ranked fourth in the world and first in Asia in the Marsh CFA Institute Global Pension Index 2026, released on 20 October 2026.
Singapore scored 82.0 out of 100, earning an A grade alongside just five other systems.
The Netherlands topped the index with 85.8, followed by Denmark (84.1) and Iceland (84.0). Israel and Australia completed the A-grade group.
The index assessed 55 retirement income systems on three measures:
Adequacy (40% weighting)
Sustainability (35%)
Integrity (25%)
It measures the overall strength of each system rather than comparing individual pension payouts.
Singapore finished well ahead of its regional peers.
Hong Kong ranked 17th, Malaysia 35th and Japan 39th, while Thailand, Indonesia and the Philippines were all in the bottom 10.
The US placed 33rd.
A strong national system does not guarantee every individual a comfortable retirement, however. Depending on their goals, investors may still need their own savings and investments.

title: Anthropic IPO set to cap year of record-breaking equity megadeals
article:
(Nov 14): Anthropic PBC is poised to add to a blockbuster year of transactions that are orders of magnitude larger than those seen in the past decade, with the biggest initial public offering (IPO) of all time joining a half dozen other jumbo equity deals.

If Anthropic’s first-time share sale prices at the top of its marketed range on Nov 18, the artificial intelligence (AI) lab’s IPO and private placement would together raise US$90.4 billion ($116.4 billion), easily surpassing the US$86.2 billion in Elon Musk’s SpaceX listing in June.

Exercising the so-called over-allotment option after the trading begins, bringing it to more than US$100 billion, would surpass Meta Platforms Inc’s roughly US$98 billion equity deal announced last month, also to fund its AI business.

More than US$425 billion has been raised across US-listed companies when accounting for IPOs, completed at-the-market share sale programmes and marketed share sales, according to data compiled by Bloomberg. That tops the 2021 total of roughly US$408 billion raised, the data showed.

Including Anthropic, the US’ three biggest-ever IPOs landed in a matter of months of each other, a sign of how deals are being turbocharged by AI companies’ need for cash on a scale never seen before. Even adjusted for inflation, this year’s biggest IPOs are far larger than previous record-holders like Saudi Aramco and Visa Inc.

While SK Hynix Inc’s US$26.5 billion US listing in July marked the largest for a company based outside of the country, its size after adjusting for inflation is actually more in line with deals from decades ago. By that measure, the South Korean company’s US first-time share sale trails debuts from Alibaba Group Holding Ltd in 2014 and SoftBank Corp in 2018.

See also: IOIPG REIT lowers IPO price to 91 sen, public tranche oversubscribed 0.59 times

The hunt for AI funding has not only broken records, it has also prompted a handful of tech giants to sell stock for the first time in decades.

Meta, led by Mark Zuckerberg, would likely hold the title for the biggest equity fundraise with its US$98 billion of offerings including a marketed stock sale and preferred shares. The bulk of the total comes in the form of a planned US$60 billion at-the-market share sale programme, which allows companies to periodically sell shares in the open market.

See also: Anthropic’s IPO is about six times oversubscribed — Bloomberg

Like IPOs, ATMs have metastasised in the AI era. Bitcoin treasury firm Strategy Inc raised US$21 billion in 2024 via an ATM and did another of the same size in 2025, data compiled by Bloomberg showed.

This year, Alphabet Inc’s roughly US$85 billion funding plan includes a US$40 billion ATM programme. Oracle Corp sold roughly US$20 billion of shares through an ATM programme, on top of raising tens of billions of dollars through the sale of additional equity and debt.

title: US stocks close lower after Nvidia spurs volatility in AI trade
article:
(Nov 14): US equities fell on Friday at the end of a volatile week as investors reassessed the artificial intelligence (AI) trade in the wake of turmoil at Nvidia Corp and the outlook of Federal Reserve (Fed) interest rates.

The tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 dropped 1.2% Friday, while the S&P 500 Index closed lower by 0.4%. Still, both gauges managed to end the week with gains. The blue-chip Dow Jones Industrial Average closed up 0.1%.

Nvidia had its worst week since the April 2025 tariff sell-off, erasing over half a trillion dollars in value this week alone, to take its market capitalisation below US$4 trillion ($5.2 trillion) after chief executive officer Jensen Huang was ousted. Confidence in the world’s biggest maker of AI-powered chips was rocked by revelations of Huang’s extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy.

Concerns around the future of Nvidia’s leadership collided with investor questions regarding the cost of funding the broader AI buildout. “We’re seeing a few different factors weighing on chip and data-centre names today,” wrote Nicole Tanenbaum, partner and chief investment officer at Chequers Financial Management. “The first is clearly the uncertainty surrounding Nvidia’s leadership transition, which could have broader implications for the AI ecosystem.”

Stocks of Nvidia’s suppliers extended a sell-off and even the chipmaker’s rivals, including Broadcom Inc and Advanced Micro Devices Inc, tumbled Friday after rallying a day earlier.

Investors will come face-to-face with the possibility that more issues may come to light surrounding Huang’s departure and the suspected spy scandal, especially as Nvidia is scheduled to report third-quarter earnings after the bell Tuesday. Angelo Zino, senior vice president at CFRA Research, said that while he expects the company’s earnings to be “perfectly fine”, the bigger risk is what the market doesn’t know yet.

See also: US stocks bounce as Nvidia rout spurs gains elsewhere

“There’s a lot there that we’re probably going to discover that we don’t want to know about,” Zino said on Bloomberg Radio.

Other areas of the AI trade are attracting attention. Orders for Anthropic’s IPO are six times oversubscribed despite the recent agitation, while CoreWeave Inc recently announced plans to raise at least US$4 billion through an investment-grade loan offering.

Still, some investors are viewing this week’s volatility as part of a rotation that’s been unfolding long before Nvidia captured headlines. “This rotation has been underway for the better part of two years,” said Chris Galipeau, head market strategist for the Franklin Templeton Institute, on Bloomberg Television. “We’ll continue to see high levels of volatility,” he added, noting his belief that the rotation is “closer to the end than the beginning”.

See also: US stocks climb as Wall Street gets fresh AI fuel

In Galipeau’s view, the most accurate long-term test for AI companies will be seen in the relationship between how much each spends on infrastructure versus the return on that particular investment. “That’s where the puck is going,” Galipeau said.

Investors got some relief early Friday, after the latest inflation data eased the risk of the Fed raising interest rates by half a percentage point next month. The producer price index rose 0.3% in October over the previous month and 6.5% over the previous year, the fastest pace in four years, but slightly below expectations. That helped take some air out of December rate-hike bets, which were fuelled by hotter-than-expected consumer prices earlier this week.

“There’s no urgency to go to 50,” said Priya Misra, managing director and portfolio manager at JP Morgan Investment Management. A half-point move could lead to a “huge messaging problem” leading Wall Street to price a neutral rate that is much higher, Misra said.

Oil is holding onto its gains, with West Texas Intermediate hovering at around US$89. The International Energy Agency said on Friday that the oil market will be in surplus this quarter for the first time since the war began.
